_doc: COST-GUARD-1 and CRITICALITY-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-13). Standing goal and measured cost findings as data; foundation/cost.py reads them (python3 -m foundation cost --check|--probe|--guard). Priority order: ultrastable works and deploys its own workers, then cost, then new features.

standing_goal.north_star: Ultrastable's loops produce more verified deploys than they consume in cost and attention.

findings.cause: fleet_tick has 67 AFTER INSERT triggers, each scanning views; one tick insert reads ~860k rows (156 inserts/day cost 134M rows); a no-op guarded insert from qnfo-code-orchestrator still reads ~150k rows per call
findings.remedy: gate triggers on NEW.source = the canonical tick source and on the 10-minute mark; move metric refresh to the hourly step; make the guarded insert a SELECT on idx_fleet_tick_source_ts first

findings.cause: reach_signals rollup query joins MAX(date) subselect per call (52k rows per call, 3571 calls/day)
findings.remedy: cache per hour in ops_config or maintain a rollup table

findings.cause: alerts lookup wraps created_at in datetime(), which defeats idx_alerts_source_created (9.4k rows per call, 4130 calls/day)
findings.remedy: compare created_at to a precomputed ISO bound, or add index alerts(source, datetime(created_at)) (migration written, not applied: production DB write was refused by the permission check)
findings.migration: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_alerts_source_dt ON alerts (source, datetime(created_at))

findings.cause: code_tasks lookup uses goal LIKE ? OR id = ? (2k rows per call, 19k calls/day)
findings.remedy: query by id first, LIKE only when no id hit

findings.ai: gpt-oss-120b, glm-5.3 and glm-5.3-flash take 52 percent of neurons
findings.remedy: route classification and routine loops to smaller models; cap per-model share

closing_probe: python3 -m foundation cost --guard (breach files a queue item; passes when every database and the AI total are under budget for the last full day)
